name: EWA Global Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own top prize under two names across its life — the Extreme World Championship at launch in 1998, renamed Global Heavyweight by the 1999 relaunch. JD Freeman won the inaugural Extreme World title in an eight-man tournament at the fed's first pay-per-view and retired from it undefeated soon after; the belt sat vacant through the rest of the captured 1998-99 run and was still listed vacant on the fed's own 3 June 1999 rankings page.

name: EWA North American Championship
epitaph: The fed's own #2 title, billed as the North American 'Cyber' Championship in its early weeks before the qualifier dropped. It changed hands four times across the captured 1998-99 run — Lonewolf, then The Train (Wayne Rothschild), then The Multinational Rebel, then Johnny Sledge — and was vacant again on the fed's own 3 June 1999 rankings page.

name: EWA Television Championship
epitaph: Billed by the fed's own rules as its 'Ironman' belt, defended weekly. Its captured lineage runs from Ray Simmons through Capital Punishment, Suicide King, Tommy Grayson and Roadkill across the fed's 1998-99 run, and was vacant again by the 3 June 1999 rankings page.

name: EWA Global Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The fed's hardcore-stipulation belt. Ronny Wonder was announced champion on 22 November 1998, the same broadcast that also announced Richard Riley as champion in what the show's own text plays as a joke rather than a clean handoff; Cyris held the belt clearly from 6 December 1998 through at least the end of that year. It was vacant again on the fed's own 3 June 1999 rankings page.

name: EWA Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Contested under a 230-pound limit. Dean McGrath became the inaugural champion at the 31 October 1998 Devil's Night; the belt passed to 'Maverick' Matt Blanchard, then Tyrant, then Shawn Foster across the captured run, and was vacant again by the fed's own 3 June 1999 rankings page.

name: EWA World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Vacant on the fed's own 3 June 1999 rankings page.
